anomalies.obs: On the CAN BUS sheet both MCP2515 CAN controllers have their SPI data pins wired cross-wise: the SI pin (serial input, 'Peripheral In') is connected to the net CAN_CIPO, and the SO pin (serial output, 'Peripheral Out') is connected to the net CAN_COPI. The same swap appears on U8 (CAN0) and U9 (CAN1).
anomalies.expected: SI (peripheral input) must carry the controller's output line CAN_COPI, and SO (peripheral output) must carry the controller's input line CAN_CIPO. This is the convention the board itself uses on the SC16IS752 UARTs (U13 pin12 'A1/SI' = SERIAL_COPI, pin13 'SD' = SERIAL_CIPO) and matches the SPI naming note and the CM4 pinout (GPIO9=CAN_COPI=MOSI out, GPIO10=CAN_CIPO=MISO in).

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet: U8 (MCP2515-xSO) left pins 14 SI -> CAN_CIPO, 15 SO -> CAN_COPI, 16 CS -> CAN_CS0, 13 SCK -> CAN_SCK; U9 (MCP2515-xSO) 14 SI -> CAN_CIPO, 15 SO -> CAN_COPI, 16 CS -> CAN_CS1, 13 SCK -> CAN_SCK
Serial sheet: U13 SC16IS752 pin12 'A1/SI' -> SERIAL_COPI, pin13 'SD' -> SERIAL_CIPO (correct master<->peripheral direction)
SPI Naming Note: COPI 'Controller Out, Peripheral In' CIPO 'Controller In, Peripheral Out'

anomalies.impact: MOSI and MISO are reversed on both CAN SPI buses, so the CM4 cannot communicate with either MCP2515; CAN0 and CAN1 (the motor/actuator interface) would be non-functional. This is not one of the documented open questions (which concern crystal value and LED polarity), so it is a deviation from the intended design.

parsed.summary: The drawing otherwise matches the spec (16 MHz crystals on Y1/Y2, e-stop sink chain U15/U22/U35/U36, LTC4412+P-MOS ideal diode U6/Q1, SM712 TVS arrays, direct SW1->GLOBAL_EN). The one clear deviation is that both MCP2515 CAN controllers have their SPI SI/SO pins swapped relative to the CAN_COPI/CAN_CIPO nets, contradicting the board's own SPI naming convention and its correctly-wired SC16IS752 UARTs, which would break SPI to the CAN hardware.
